messages:
Jordan (Support): heads up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 generation spikes and 429s starting ~09:10 UTC. They see long queue times and request timeouts. attaching short repro + logs. :frowning:

Maya (Support): thanks — any common tenant or model? can you paste a sample request id?

Jordan (Support): two tenants: tenant-phi-21, tenant-alpha-7. sample request id: req_20260317_09_14_331. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T09:13:55Z] ingress: admit_delay_ms=4200, queue_len=1200, served_workers=18, concurrency_limit=16, tenant=tenant-phi-21, model=redwood-rt-medium
[2026-03-17T09:14:01Z] rpc: error=admit_throttled, status=429, req=req_20260317_09_14_331
```

Tom (SRE): :eyes: that queue_len and concurrency_limit mismatch stands out. Did we recently lower worker pool or change per-model concurrency?

Lee (Eng Runtime): we had a mixed-mode autoscale patch merged in last night that tightened active shards per model to reduce cost for small tenants. I rolled that out to canary but looks like it went wide. patch: "autoscale: max_shards_per_model=2, target_util=0.65"

Maya (Support): customers say it started exactly after ~09:05 UTC — matches rollout. escalation is for user-facing latency / 429s. Need fast mitigation and repro steps.

Tom (SRE): mitigation options (fast to apply):
- bump per-model concurrency for the affected pool (hotfix)
- enable fallback: route to a higher-capacity model variant (redwood-rt-large) for these tenants
- temporarily raise worker pool for cluster "eu-west-1-a"
Choose 1+2 for fastest customer impact.

Lee (Eng Runtime): agree. I can push a hotfix to increase concurrency_limit to 48 for redwood-rt-medium in the affected cluster. doing a config change, will keep it scoped to tenants with >100 rps.

ingress-bot: alert: admission_control.rate=HIGH, cluster=eu-west-1-a, affected_tenants=[tenant-phi-21,tenant-alpha-7], p99_latency_ms=2540

Jordan (Support): repro steps for engineers:
1) set header X-Tenant=tenant-phi-21
2) run the following to simulate steady concurrent requests (100 concurrent):
```
hey -n 10000 -c 100 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-medium","input":"hello world"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Expected: queue backlog grows and 429s appear when concurrency_limit reached.

Tom (SRE): I'm already scaling the worker pool up by +4 nodes for eu-west-1-a and patching concurrency_limit. Lee — please patch runtime config and post PR link. I'll monitor admission metrics.

Lee (Eng Runtime): pushing hotfix now — patch id: rtm-20260317-042. Applying to cluster...

Lee (Eng Runtime): patch applied. config now: concurrency_limit=48 for redwood-rt-medium (scoped). rolling restart of 6 workers staged.

Tom (SRE): seeing drop in queue_len: was ~1200 -> now ~150 within 2 mins. p95 dropped from 1200ms -> 230ms in the dashboards. continuing to watch.

Maya (Support): updated customers (tenant-phi-21, tenant-alpha-7) and asked them to confirm.

Jordan (Support): customer confirmation: tenant-phi-21 reports p99 back to normal, no more 429s. tenant-alpha-7 also seeing improvement. closing for now but leaving monitoring on. thanks team. :raised_hands:

Tom (SRE): follow-ups (action items):
- Lee: revert autoscale hardening change in canary and prepare a safer rollout (include gradual ramp + traffic test) — owner: Lee, due EOD
- Eng: add per-tenant retry/fanout metrics to alert rules so we detect fairness regressions earlier — owner: Tom, due +2 days
- Support: compile customer impact notes for postmortem — owner: Maya, due +1 day

Jordan (Support): filing a short incident summary and tagging affected customers. will attach logs + timeline to #postmortems if anything else comes up.

Maya (Support): :white_check_mark: thanks everyone.
